seed_cauchy_summable_differences: Strategy: show (a_n) is Cauchy. For m > n, by the triangle inequality |a_m - a_n| <= sum_{k=n}^{m-1} |a_{k+1}-a_k| <= sum_{k=n}^{m-1} 1/2^k < 1/2^{n-1}. Given eps>0 pick N with 1/2^{N-1} < eps; then |a_m - a_n| < eps for all m>n>=N, so (a_n) is Cauchy. Since R is complete, (a_n) converges.
seed_iterated_map_to_zero: Strategy: monotone convergence then identify the limit. If x_0=0 the sequence is constantly 0. If x_0>0, induction with f:[0,1]->[0,1] and f(x)<x on (0,1] gives 0 < x_{n+1}=f(x_n) < x_n, so (x_n) is strictly decreasing and bounded below by 0, hence converges to some L>=0. By continuity L=f(L); if L>0 then f(L)<L, a contradiction, so L=0.
seed_periodic_two_critical_points: Strategy: Rolle plus extreme values. Periodicity gives f(0)=f(1), so by Rolle there is c1 in (0,1) with f'(c1)=0. Since f is continuous, periodic and non-constant, it attains a maximum and a minimum; choosing representatives in [0,1) (shift by a period if an extremum lands on an endpoint) these occur at distinct interior points x1 != x2, where f'(x1)=f'(x2)=0. That gives at least two distinct zeros of f' in [0,1).
seed_nonneg_zero_integral: Strategy: contradiction via continuity. Suppose f(c)>0 for some c. By continuity there is an interval I around c (of length L>0, inside [0,1]) on which f >= f(c)/2 > 0. Then integral over [0,1] of f >= integral over I of f >= (f(c)/2)*L > 0, contradicting that the integral is 0. Hence f(x)=0 for all x.
seed_cauchy_functional_equation: Strategy: build up rationals then use continuity. Set x=y=0: f(0)=0. Induction gives f(nx)=n f(x); f(-x)=-f(x); so f(qx)=q f(x) for rational q. With c=f(1), f(q)=cq for all rational q. Since f is continuous and x->cx agrees with f on the dense rationals, f(x)=cx for all real x.
seed_recursive_sequence_limit: Strategy: contraction to a fixed point. By induction 0<a_n<=1. The candidate limit solves L=1/(2+L), i.e. L^2+2L-1=0, L=sqrt(2)-1. Since |a_{n+1}-L| = |a_n-L| / ((2+a_n)(2+L)) <= |a_n-L|/4, the map is a contraction, so a_n -> L = sqrt(2)-1.
seed_uniform_limit_continuous: Strategy: the eps/3 argument. Fix x_0 and eps>0. By uniform convergence choose N with |f_N(x)-f(x)| < eps/3 for all x. By continuity of f_N at x_0 choose delta with |f_N(x)-f_N(x_0)| < eps/3 when |x-x_0|<delta. Then |f(x)-f(x_0)| <= |f(x)-f_N(x)| + |f_N(x)-f_N(x_0)| + |f_N(x_0)-f(x_0)| < eps. So f is continuous at x_0.
seed_derivative_limit_average: Strategy: Mean Value Theorem on [M,x]. Given eps>0 pick M with |f'(t)-L|<eps for t>M. For x>M, MVT gives f(x)-f(M)=f'(xi)(x-M) for some xi in (M,x). Then f(x)/x = f(M)/x + f'(xi)*(x-M)/x. As x->infinity, f(M)/x -> 0 and (x-M)/x -> 1, while f'(xi) stays within eps of L. Hence f(x)/x -> L.
seed_contraction_unique_fixed_point: Strategy: contraction mapping. Uniqueness: if f(p)=p and f(q)=q then |p-q|=|f(p)-f(q)|<=k|p-q|, so (1-k)|p-q|<=0, forcing p=q. Existence: iterate x_{n+1}=f(x_n); then |x_{n+1}-x_n|<=k^n|x_1-x_0|, so the tails form a geometric bound and (x_n) is Cauchy, hence converges to some p; continuity gives f(p)=p.
seed_gronwall_zero_function: Strategy: Gronwall-type bound. For x in [0,a] with a<1, f(0)=0 gives f(x)=integral_0^x f'(t) dt, so |f(x)| <= integral_0^x |f(t)| dt <= M_a * x <= M_a * a, where M_a = max over [0,a] of |f|. Taking the max over [0,a] gives M_a <= M_a * a, so (1-a) M_a <= 0, hence M_a = 0. Thus f=0 on [0,a] for every a<1, so f=0 on [0,1].
